correctness.rationale: Rebuilt the independent smallest-letter insertion process: B_j are independent Bernoulli(1/j) indicators of a new initial record, and D_j=D_{j-1}+(1-B_j)1{U_j>D_{j-1}/(j-1)}. Conditioning the B-vector on its total admits a coordinatewise monotone coupling by induction and Newton log-concavity; the update is antitone in B and monotone in integer D, proving every tail inequality. Strictness follows from positive probability of the final B_n changing and a positive last descent increment. Independent covariance recursion gives C_j=(1-1/j)C_{j-1}-1/(2j), hence the asserted value. Independent exact joint recurrence and tail checks through n=9, direct permutation enumeration through n=7 corroborate but do not prove the infinite statement.

value.rationale: A complete stochastic regression order between two fundamental permutation statistics is materially stronger than a single negative covariance, applies to every increasing function of total descent count, and has an explicit explanatory coupling; it is a natural all-n structural dependence theorem, not a restated joint enumerator.

final_claim: For every uniform one-line permutation size n>=2, descents conditioned on r left-to-right records strictly decrease in first-order stochastic order as r rises from 1 to n; Cov(D_n,R_n)=-(n-1)/(2n).
